title: Contrasting anisotropic electron-phonon-spin coupling in Fe$_{3}$GeTe$_{2}$ and Fe$_{5}$GeTe$_{2}$: A helicity-resolved Raman study
authors: Smrutiranjan Mekap, Jyoti Saini, Andrzej Ptok, Pawan Kumar Srivastava, Changgu Lee, Subhasis Ghosh, Anushree Roy
abstract: Two-dimensional van der Waals ferromagnets Fe$_3$GeTe$ _2$ (F3GT) and Fe$_5$GeTe$_2$ (F5GT) exhibit pronounced magneto-optical responses, which open promising platforms for investigating the interplay among lattice, electronic, and magnetic degrees of freedom. Here, we present a comparative study of optical resonance-induced anisotropic electron-phonon coupling and its association with magnetic ordering in these systems using wavelength- and temperature-dependent helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy. By resolving the doubly degenerate E modes under left- and right-circularly polarized excitations, we demonstrate that the temperature evolution of the chiral mode splitting ($Δf$) does not track the magnetization behavior, indicating that the helicity-dependent Raman response arises not solely from time-reversal symmetry breaking due to magnetic order, but also from spin-orbit-coupled electronic interactions. Notably, in F3GT, the out-of-plane magnetization indirectly governs the in-plane anisotropic electron-phonon coupling under optical resonance, whereas F5GT exhibits static anisotropic interactions. The Fano asymmetry parameter $1/q$ reveals mode- and temperature-dependent coupling strengths between phonons and the electronic continuum, with pronounced angular anisotropy in F3GT but isotropic behavior in F5GT--- a consequence of its multiple Fe sites and enhanced interlayer hybridization in the latter. Our results demonstrate the role of crystal structure and magnetic anisotropy in shaping the anisotropically coupled electron-phonon-spin dynamics in these layered metallic ferromagnets, and highlight Fe$_x$GeTe$_2$ as a versatile platform for microscopic insight into chiral light-matter interactions in layered metallic ferromagnets.
summary: The research uses helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy to compare the electron-phonon-spin coupling in $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{GeTe}_2$ and $	ext{Fe}_5	ext{GeTe}_2$. The findings reveal that this coupling is complex, stemming from spin-orbit interactions rather than just magnetic ordering. This highlights how crystal structure dictates the nature of anisotropic light-matter interaction in these layered magnets.
main_problem: The study aims to comparatively investigate anisotropic electron-phonon-spin coupling mechanisms in two-dimensional van der Waals ferromagnets, $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{GeTe}_2$ and $	ext{Fe}_5	ext{GeTe}_2$.
main_result: The helicity-dependent Raman response is shown to arise from spin-orbit-coupled electronic interactions rather than solely from time-reversal symmetry breaking due to magnetic order. Furthermore, the crystal structure dictates distinct coupling behaviors between the two compounds.
method: Helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy was employed, utilizing left- and right-circularly polarized excitations across varying temperatures and wavelengths.
model_or_system: The physical systems are layered metallic ferromagnets: $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{GeTe}_2$ (hexagonal) and $	ext{Fe}_5	ext{GeTe}_2$ (rhombohedral). The analysis focuses on the interplay between lattice vibrations, electronic structure, and magnetic ordering in these materials.
key_observables: Chiral mode splitting ($\Delta f$), Fano asymmetry parameter ($1/q$), and polarization-dependent Raman intensities derived from helicity-resolved measurements.
important_parameters: Temperature dependence of coupling strengths; the difference between out-of-plane vs. in-plane magnetization effects on coupling anisotropy.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed spectral features can be decomposed into contributions from electron-phonon, spin-orbit, and magnetic ordering effects using symmetry group theory for Raman tensor fitting.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate unit cells for both compounds; polarization dependence plots (e.g., in VH configuration) are used to analyze mode symmetries and coupling mechanisms.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the context of 2D van der Waals ferromagnets, details the comparative measurements on $	ext{F}3	ext{GT}$ and $	ext{F}5	ext{GT}$, presents spectroscopic evidence regarding chiral splitting and Fano parameters, and concludes by relating structural differences to distinct coupling dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides experimental insight into how lattice vibrations couple anisotropically with spin-orbit coupled electronic states in magnetic materials, which is crucial for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter systems.
